case_name: Muthu Naicker and Others v State of Tamil Nadu
respondent:
State of Tamil Nadu
Supreme Court of India

10 August 1978
Cr.A. Nos. 230 and 238 of 1972 and 97 of 1973.
The Judgment was delivered by: DESAI, J.
1.  These three appeals arise out of the judgment rendered by a Division Bench of the High Court of Madras in Criminal Appeal 295 of 1970 convicting 27 appellants for different offences, who were acquitted of all charged levelled against them by the learned Sessions Judge, Chingleput Division in Sessions Case 25 of 1969 in which 28 persons were put up for trial for various offences including the one under Section 302/34, Indian Penal Code against accused 1 to 10, 16, 17, 19 and 20, and under Section 302/149, IPC against rest of the accused and 37 other charges for specific offences under Sections 323, 324, 325 and read with S. 149 and S. 427 read with Section 34, IPC.

court_reasoning: Unfortunately, in respect of those accused who have been convicted for an offence under Section 302/34, IPC, there is an appeal to this Court as of right, but in appeals by special leave ordinarily this Court does not undertake to reappreciate evidence.
holding: The trial of the accused resulted in acquittal and in appeal by the State, the Court reached the conclusion as hereinbefore recorded.
